decisions.premise_reviewed: CalGray/CalRGB are converted through CIE XYZ and the shared XYZ-to-sRGB path; BlackPoint is retained but not applied in the current rendering policy.
decisions.source_check: ISO 32000-2 §8.6.5.2–.3 Tables 62–63 and transform definitions, printed pp. 186–188; §10.3 governs conversion and was not audited here. The source says BlackPoint and WhitePoint control gamut mapping, while the detailed conversion behavior is chapter 10.
decisions.assessment: The numeric assertions and code path substantiate the selected source-space transforms; the policy not to apply Cal-space BlackPoint is outside this bounded conversion audit and should not be upgraded to a §8.6-only requirement.

decisions.premise_reviewed: The ledger correction states Table 62/63/64 WhitePoint requires positive X/Z and Y=1, while parser enforces positivity of all components but not Y=1.
decisions.source_check: Table 62 printed p. 186, Table 63 printed p. 187, Table 64 printed p. 189. Y=1 is a producer constraint. The selected text does not require the reader to reject or normalize a nonconforming WhitePoint.
decisions.assessment: Ledger correction accurately distinguishes stated constraint from code validation. The ADR's acceptance of scaled Y values is reader recovery/policy; no conformance defect is established by acceptance alone. The table does require nonnegative BlackPoint entries, which the selected code review did not independently trace.

decisions.premise_reviewed: An ICCBased source profile must reach the same colour conversion path for fills and images, with /Alternate only as fallback when the profile cannot be applied.
decisions.source_check: Table 65 and source-space paragraphs printed pp. 191–193; the image route itself is outside this shard.
decisions.assessment: The same-profile fill/image regression is a strong observable control. Table 65's ICCBased-to-Alternate Range clamp is an unasserted requirement: a later ICC.2 v5 Lab display profile with mpet A2B0/B2A0 transforms was generated and accepted by ICC's official iccDEV 2.3.2.5 conformance validator. The exact-xref consumer test comparing ICC-range clamp to wider Alternate Lab remains an unexecuted draft; parent integration/run decides behavior. This is not a passed product regression yet.

decisions.premise_reviewed: Sample/default ranges must follow each colour space's own range; ICC Lab uses the Table 68 range rather than unit normalization.
decisions.source_check: Table 68 printed p. 193; `Profile::component_range` and direct ICC range tests use [0,100] and [-128,127].
decisions.assessment: Supported by current ICC unit tests. The Indexed-over-Lab portion mentioned in this ADR is §8.6.6.3 and excluded from this shard.

decisions.premise_reviewed: Each ICC component's default range and explicit /Range affect sample interpretation.
decisions.source_check: Table 65/68 and Table 88; Table 88/image Decode are outside current scope, while the ICC source-range rules are in scope.
decisions.assessment: ICC-specific assertions substantiate the component ranges; no assertion review here of image Decode consumer semantics.

decisions.premise_reviewed: The ICC version table is keyed to profile header versions (2.x and 4.x), not the PDF version.
decisions.source_check: Effective ISO+EC3 PDF printed pp. 191–192 / physical pp. 206–207. The adjacent text requires ICC.1:2010 reader support and says writers may embed earlier or later ICC versions; errata-read.md records #181 at both table pages.
decisions.assessment: `icc.rs` reads the ICC header version byte and distinguishes pre-v4 encoding from v4+; it does not key profile interpretation to PDF version. The selected tests exercise v2/v4 profiles, not a v5 profile. ICC.2 v5 is explicitly a later profile version; Table 65's later-version paragraph applies if a processor cannot process it.

unreviewed: Other ADRs governing output intents, device defaults, device CMYK conversion and chapter 10 conversions.
